title: Language membership and bounded configuration reachability
statement: Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes and a finite state set, and suppose $N$ decides a language $L$ within space bound $\mathrm{sp}$. Let $x$ be a Boolean string, and let $s,w\in\mathbb{N}$. Write $q$ for the number of states of $N$, set $d=2\bigl(3(q+1)+3k+1\bigr)+2$, and define $B=3(q+1)(|x|+2)3^{k(2s+1)}(2s+1)^k$. If $\mathrm{sp}(|x|)\le s$, $d\bigl(s+\lfloor\log_2|x|\rfloor+2\bigr)\le w$, and $B\le 2^w$, then $x\in L$ if and only if there are natural numbers $u,v<2^w$ whose encodings with $x$ and $s$ represent, respectively, the initial configuration and an accepting configuration of $N$, and $v$ is reachable from $u$ through the encoded one-step configuration relation at recursive depth $w$, with intermediate codes less than $2^w$.
